headline: Health Minister finds expired medicines in toilet at Morrelganj health complex
summary: Minister Sardar Sakhavat Hossain discovered medical supplies and expired drugs worth lakhs of taka in a toilet and abandoned building during a surprise visit.
details: Health Minister Sardar Sakhavat Hossain expressed anger over mismanagement at the Morrelganj Upazila Health Complex in Bagerhat during a surprise visit on Saturday.
During the inspection, the Minister found expired medicines worth lakhs of taka scattered in an abandoned building and medical equipment, including saline and syringes, lying in an unused toilet.

The Minister also discovered that the Upazila Health and Family Planning Officer (THO) Kamal Hossain Mufti owns a private clinic right next to the hospital, which the Minister confirmed upon visiting the site.
A check of biometric attendance records revealed that several doctors were regularly arriving late to the hospital.

When the Minister called the Bagerhat Civil Surgeon, Dr. Mahbubul Alam, he claimed to be on leave with verbal permission from the Khulna Divisional Health Director, but the Director denied knowing about the leave.
The Minister stated that the government's goal is to ensure proper healthcare for poor people with limited means, and the hospital's capacity will soon be increased from 50 to 101 beds.
Minister Sakhavat Hossain noted that he has documented all the irregularities and will take necessary action after discussing with higher authorities in Dhaka.
Following the Morrelganj visit, the Minister also visited the Sharankhola Upazila Health Complex, where he expressed satisfaction with the overall healthcare services.
caption:
Expired medicines in a toilet? Health Minister discovers shocking mismanagement at Morrelganj health complex.

Health Minister Sardar Sakhavat Hossain expressed anger over mismanagement at the Morrelganj Upazila Health Complex in Bagerhat during a surprise visit on Saturday.

During the inspection, the Minister found expired medicines worth lakhs of taka scattered in an abandoned building and medical equipment, including saline and syringes, lying in an unused toilet.

The Minister also discovered that the Upazila Health and Family Planning Officer (THO) Kamal Hossain Mufti owns a private clinic right next to the hospital, which the Minister confirmed upon visiting the site.

A check of biometric attendance records revealed that several doctors were regularly arriving late to the hospital.

When the Minister called the Bagerhat Civil Surgeon, Dr. Mahbubul Alam, he claimed to be on leave with verbal permission from the Khulna Divisional Health Director, but the Director denied knowing about the leave.

The Minister stated that the government's goal is to ensure proper healthcare for poor people with limited means, and the hospital's capacity will soon be increased from 50 to 101 beds.

Minister Sakhavat Hossain noted that he has documented all the irregularities and will take necessary action after discussing with higher authorities in Dhaka.

Following the Morrelganj visit, the Minister also visited the Sharankhola Upazila Health Complex, where he expressed satisfaction with the overall healthcare services.
